gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 20 W USB-C port on the Anker 351 (A9192), ChatGPT's 'best overall value' pick in both chats, only gives 20 W when both USB-A ports are empty, since the two USB-A ports share 5 V/3 A, so it charges phones but not laptops; nor do they state APC's rule that plugging a non-APC surge strip into an APC UPS's output can void its Equipment Protection Policy.
standout_why: I compared against honestfred.com (it names the Anker 351 with 2,100 J but gives no USB-C wattage or port-sharing condition and says nothing about UPSs or power stations) and against ChatGPT's own answers, which call USB-C 'useful for phone and tablet charging' and repeat the cited Illinois guide's general 'plug strips directly into wall outlets, not into other strips'. That covers daisy-chaining in general, but not the Anker port-sharing limit, the UPS warranty effect or the 1,250 W cap on TESSAN strips. I could not read the two cited pages: tomsguide.com came back almost empty (121 characters) and goodhousekeeping.com blocked the fetch, so either may carry the Anker USB-C figure. That is why this is a 2 and not a 3.
decides: It confirms the Anker 351 as a value AC strip but rules it out as a laptop or multi-device USB charger. It gives 20 W from USB-C only with the USB-A ports empty, so a shopper who wants USB-C laptop charging needs a separate GaN charger plugged into one of its outlets. For shoppers who own a UPS or a power station, it adds a rule: plug the UPS into the wall and the strip into the wall, never the strip into the UPS output (APC). Anker SOLIX says the same and allows only a strip without surge protection on a UPS. TESSAN's PS07 strips cap AC at 1,250 W, against 1,875 W on the Anker, so a 1,500 W appliance is over its limit.

findings.label: When the USB-C port gives its full 20 W
findings.value: 20 W (PIQ 3.0) only when both USB-A ports are not in use
findings.note: The maker's US page says: '20W USB-C charging is only available when the 2 USB-A ports are not in use.' 20 W is a phone or tablet rate, well below the 45 to 100 W most laptops draw over USB-C. The page does not say what the USB-C port gives when a USB-A port is in use.

findings.label: USB-A output
findings.value: 2 ports, 5 V/3 A (15 W) total, 2.4 A max per port
findings.note: 15 W = 5 V × 3 A, shared by both USB-A ports.

findings.label: Max AC load and price
findings.note: The $28.99 price is from Anker's US store and matches the Walmart price ChatGPT showed. The page does not state the cord length.

findings.label: Surge strip, power strip or extension cord on a UPS output
findings.value: Not recommended for all Back-UPS and Smart-UPS models. A non-APC surge protector, power strip or extension cord on an APC UPS output can void the Equipment Protection Policy; the standard 3-year product warranty is kept. An APC-brand strip keeps both.
findings.source_title: Using surge strips with APC's Back-UPS and Smart-UPS products (FA158852), last modified 4/1/2026
findings.note: Reasons the FAQ gives: the strip can hide part of the load from the UPS, a UPS plugged into a surge strip may switch to battery more often, and the ground the UPS needs for surge protection can be compromised. It tells you to plug the UPS straight into the wall and use a PDU for more outlets.

findings.label: Power strip on a battery backup
findings.value: Only a strip without surge protection. 'You can plug a power strip into a UPS, but only if it does not have surge protection.'
findings.source_title: Can You Plug a Surge Protector into a Battery Backup: 2026 Answers (Anker SOLIX, 2026-07-05)
findings.note: Anker SOLIX says two protectors can 'compete', send the UPS to battery when it doesn't need to and wear the battery faster. For power stations the article only says to avoid extra power strips 'unless explicitly approved by the manufacturer'.

findings.label: Max AC load and USB output
findings.value: 8 AC outlets, up to 1,250 W in total; 2× USB-C (PD up to 20 W) + 2× USB-A (up to 12 W each); $28.99
findings.source_title: TESSAN 20W Surge Protector Power Strip PS07
findings.note: Read through storecheck.py search on tessan.com; a direct product fetch returned HTTP 429. The page gives both '2000J' and '2100J'. Its 1,250 W cap is below a 1,500 W hair dryer or heater and below the Anker 351's 1,875 W. Cord options listed: 5, 10 and 15 ft flat cord with a 0.31-inch flat plug.

findings.label: Outlet layout for bulky adapters
findings.value: 12 outlets: 8 rotating + 4 fixed; 4,320 J; 8 ft cord
findings.source_title: Getting to know the Belkin PivotPlug 12-Outlet Surge Protector, 8 ft. Cord, BP112230-08
findings.note: The Belkin support article gives no amp rating and no dollar amount for the Connected Equipment Warranty.
